message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look at the long‑weekend windows that Canadians enjoyed in 2023 (based on the federal holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday, or that are observed on the following Monday when they land on a weekend).  These are the dates you’ll see in most holiday‑planning apps for Canada in 2023:

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if weekend) | Long‑Weekend Window |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Observed Mon Jan 2 | **Jan 1 – 3** (Sun Jan 1 – Tue Jan 3) |
| Family Day (Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Feb 20 (Monday) | – | **Feb 18 – 20** (Sat Feb 18 – Mon Feb 20) |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | – | **Apr 7 – 9** (Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | – | **May 20 – 22** (Sat May 20 – Mon May 22) |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Observed Mon Jul 3 | **Jul 1 – 3** (Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3) |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | – | **Sep 2 – 4** (Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4) |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Monday) | – | **Oct 7 – 9** (Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9) |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Saturday) | Observed Mon Nov 13 | **Nov 11 – 13** (Sat Nov 11 – Mon Nov 13) |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Monday) | – | **Dec 23 – 25** (Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25) |

**Quick notes**

* If a holiday falls on a weekend, Canada typically observes it on the following Monday (unless the holiday itself is on a Saturday, in which case the holiday remains on Saturday and the Monday is a “substitute” holiday).  
* The “long‑weekend window” column shows the three‑day stretch that includes the holiday and the adjacent weekend days.  
* Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. John’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, etc.) that can also create long weekends.  The table above focuses on the federal holidays that apply nationwide.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app or use the dates directly for scheduling. Happy planning!
